newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran offers to host Afghanistan peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Iran offers to host Afghanistan peace talks.

text.p: Iran has offered to host talks to secure peace in Afghanistan, an Iranian foreign ministry official was reported on Sunday as saying.
Iranian deputy foreign minister for Asia-Pacific affairs Alaeddin Boroujerdi said the warring parties expected to attend included the Islamic movement Taleban.
"Necessary coordinations have been made in this regard but the exact dates have not been fixed yet," the English-language Tehran Times newspaper quoted Boroujerdi as saying.
"Any plan formulated abroad in the absence of all the Afghan groups and without taking into account demands of all Afghan sides is doomed to fail," Boroujerdi said.

Tehran recognises the government of ousted Afghan president Burhanuddin Rabbani and has said Taleban, which seized Kabul in September, gave Islam a bad name. But it has urged Afghan factions to reach a power-sharing agreement.

Representatives of the warring Afghan factions held three days of U.N.-sponsored talks in Pakistan last week and U.N. officials said participants had agreed to meet again next month to continue their discussions.
